Docs/Reproduction record

Reproduction record

Save enough evidence for another researcher to identify the task, checkpoint, data and protocol behind a result.

A checklist, not a submission portal

Community submission intake is not open

The current leaderboard presents the supplied manuscript baselines. This page describes reproducibility records; it does not provide an upload endpoint, announce an open competition or promise inclusion in a public ranking.

Keep experiments from different task revisions, checkpoints, instruction protocols or data subsets separately labeled. The leaderboard protocol defines how the three reported tracks are aggregated.

Record identity before running

RecordInclude
Source and taskRepository commit and local changes; current environment ID and hand; task fingerprint and any resolved lineage.
ModelMethod, checkpoint path and hash, training data subset, model/runtime versions and any pretrained Base dependency.
EnvironmentRobot UID, controller, physics backend, registered horizon, reset policy and native-scene manifest when relevant.
Policy inputs and actionsCamera preset and resolution, preprocessing, temporal offsets, state channel names, normalization and action execution rule.
EvaluationRequested seed list, number of complete episodes, instruction sampling, scene IDs and result-directory identity.

Do not replace a changed task fingerprint with the release fingerprint. Record-neutral compatibility is handled by tasks/config/fingerprint_lineage.py ↗ and must have evidence behind it.

Retain per-episode evidence

Save every requested episode's seed, success-at-any-step result, length and failure or infrastructure-error status. Preserve the evaluator CSV or episodes.jsonl, its summary, run command and diagnostic videos where available. A completed denominator matters more than an attractive aggregate percentage.

Identify ACT/DP execution settings, PPO/RLPD rendered demonstration dependencies, GR00T canonical versus registered instruction sampling and π0.5 Base/package hashes. The released GR00T multi-instruction checkpoints are not the paper's single-instruction checkpoints; do not label one as a reproduction of the other.

Aggregate only comparable runs

Average the stage-level success rates over the 30 canonical stages. For cross-scene results, calculate each scene's average first and then the mean and standard deviation across the three named scenes. Long-horizon results concern the 10 complete sequences from one reset, not the mean or product of standalone stage scores.

Keep partial diagnostic runs and workstation measurements out of these headline aggregates. Report all deviations from the fixed task, camera, horizon and seed protocol. Read Evaluation for released-package limitations and Citation for the canonical paper reference.
